haiku-low.q1: Reports of 10,000 rows or fewer stream the CSV in the click's response. Larger reports return 202 with an export record, and a background job later emails a download link.
haiku-low.q2: The server returns the existing queued or running export and starts nothing. The duplicate check ignores the view's filters.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The exports bucket deletes each object 7 days after creation. No cleanup job is built.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts. After the third fails, the handler sets status failed, saves the error and emails a failure notice. The page offers Download CSV again.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica. Report rows are never read from the main database.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row in the main database. The page polls GET /exports/current every 5 seconds while queued or running, so reopening it shows the latest state.
haiku-low.q7: It never holds the whole report. It reads batches of 500 rows and uploads 5 MB parts one at a time, holding only one batch and one part.
haiku-low.q8: After an error, the job aborts the upload, discarding its parts. After a timeout or worker death, no abort runs and the bucket's 24-hour rule discards it. The next attempt starts a new upload; earlier parts are never reused.
haiku-low.q9: The view is saved in the report_exports row at click time. The job payload carries only export_id, so the job reads the view from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A database rule allowing only one queued or running export per user and report. A refused second insert makes the server return the winning export.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be completed and visible at its key, and the export-ready email must be sent, before status becomes done. If the job reruns after done, it stops and writes no second file.

sonnet.q1: By reports.row_count: 10,000 or fewer rows streams the CSV directly as the response to the click (nothing stored). Above 10,000, the click returns 202 at once with an export_id and status; a background job builds the file, emails a link valid 24 hours, and the page shows the export state.
sonnet.q2: The server finds the user's existing queued/running export of that report (ignoring filters) and returns it instead; no new export or job starts.
sonnet.q3: The emailed link works 24 hours (the status call can return a fresh 24-hour link). The exports bucket deletes every object 7 days after creation; no cleanup job exists.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (waits of 60 s before attempt 2 and 300 s before attempt 3). After the third fails, the final-failure handler sets status failed, saves the error and sends the failure email. The page says the export failed and offers Download CSV to start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only, never the main database (which holds the export records).
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table's status column in the main database. The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/current on opening, which returns the user's most recent export for the report; while queued or running it polls every 5 seconds, stopping at done or failed. A returning user sees the state via the same call.
sonnet.q7: It streams: writes the header, reads rows from the replica in batches of 500, holds only one batch and one upload part (5 MB min) at a time, uploads each part via multipart upload keeping etags, then uploads the final part and completes. The whole report is never in memory.
sonnet.q8: If an error is raised, the job aborts that attempt's multipart upload (discarding parts), saves the error, and re-raises. On a timeout or worker death no abort runs, and the bucket's 24-hour rule discards the unfinished upload. The next attempt restarts at step 4b with a brand-new upload and the file from the beginning; earlier parts are never reused.
sonnet.q9: The view is stored in the view column of the report_exports row (the page's query string) in the main database. The job payload contains only the export_id, and the job loads the row to get the view.
sonnet.q10: A database rule allowing only one queued or running export per user and report. If the insert is refused, the server returns the winning export, as in the duplicate check.
sonnet.q11: The file must have been fully uploaded and the multipart upload completed, and a signed 24-hour link created. Only after the email is sent is the status set to done. On a rerun, the job loads the export row; if status is done it stops and writes no second file.
sonnet.q12: If reading fails partway, the response stops and the download fails; nothing is stored, and the user clicks again.
